nodes.title: Conductivity & Covalent Compounds
nodes.description: know that covalent compounds do not usually conduct electricity

nodes.title: Diffusion & Dilution
nodes.description:
understand how the results of experiments involving the dilution of coloured solutions
and diffusion of gases can be explained

nodes.title: Bases
nodes.description: know that metal oxides, metal hydroxides and ammonia can act as bases, and that alkalis are bases that are soluble in water

nodes.title: Electronic Configurations & the Periodic Table
nodes.description: understand how the electronic configuration of a main group element is related to its position in the Periodic Table

nodes.title: Predicting Properties in Group 7
nodes.description: use knowledge of trends in Group 7 to predict the properties of other halogens

nodes.title: Tests for Gases
nodes.description:
describe tests for these gases: 
• hydrogen 
• oxygen 
• carbon dioxide 
• ammonia 
• chlorine.

nodes.title: Atoms & Molecules
nodes.description: know what is meant by the terms atom and molecule

nodes.title: Representing Organic Compounds
nodes.description:
know that a hydrocarbon is a compound of hydrogen and carbon only
understand how to represent organic molecules using empirical formulae, molecular formulae, general formulae, structural formulae and displayed formulae
understand how to write the possible structural and displayed formulae of an organic molecule given its molecular formula

nodes.title: Covalent Bonds: Dot & Cross Diagrams
nodes.description:
understand how to use dot-and-cross diagrams to represent covalent bonds in: 
• diatomic molecules, including hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, halogens and hydrogen halides 
• inorganic molecules including water, ammonia and carbon dioxide 
• organic molecules containing up to two carbon atoms, including methane, ethane, ethene and those containing halogen atoms.

nodes.title: Classify Metals & Non-Metals
nodes.description: understand how to use electrical conductivity and the acid-base character of oxides to classify elements as metals or non-metals

nodes.title: Acids, Bases & Protons
nodes.description:
understand acids and bases in terms of proton transfer
understand that an acid is a proton donor and a base is a proton acceptor

nodes.title: Carbon Dioxide from Thermal Decomposition
nodes.description: describe the formation of carbon dioxide from the thermal decomposition of metal carbonates, including copper(II) carbonate

nodes.title: Testing for Alkenes
nodes.description: describe how bromine water can be used to distinguish between an alkane and an alkene

nodes.title: Composition of Air
nodes.description: know the approximate percentages by volume of the four most abundant gases in dry air

nodes.title: Organic Terminology
nodes.description: know what is meant by the terms homologous series, functional group and isomerism

nodes.title: Bromine & Alkenes
nodes.description: describe the reactions of alkenes with bromine to produce dibromoalkanes

nodes.title: The Mole
nodes.description: know that the mole (mol) is the unit for the amount of a substance

nodes.title: Reactions of Acids
nodes.description: describe the reactions of hydrochloric acid, sulfuric acid and nitric acid with metals, bases and metal carbonates (excluding the reactions between nitric acid and metals) to form salts

nodes.title: Practical: Effect of Catalysts on Rate of Reaction
nodes.description: practical: investigate the effect of different solids on the catalytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide solution

nodes.title: Rusting of Iron
nodes.description: know the conditions under which iron rusts

nodes.title: Formation of Ions
nodes.description: understand how ions are formed by electron loss or gain

nodes.title: Preventing Iron Rusting
nodes.description:
understand how the rusting of iron may be prevented by: 
• barrier methods 
• galvanising 
• sacrificial protection.

nodes.title: Tests for Water
nodes.description:
describe a test for the presence of water using anhydrous copper(II) sulfate
describe a physical test to show whether a sample of water is pure

nodes.title: The Alkenes
nodes.description:
know that alkenes contain the functional group >C=C<
know the general formula for alkenes
explain why alkenes are classified as unsaturated hydrocarbons
understand how to draw the structural and displayed formulae for alkenes with up to four carbon atoms in the molecule, and name the unbranched-chain isomers knowledge of cis/trans or E/Z notation is not required

nodes.title: Displacement Reactions
nodes.description: understand how displacement reactions involving halogens and halides provide evidence for the trend in reactivity in Group 7

nodes.title: Fractional Distillation
nodes.description:
describe these experimental techniques for the separation of mixtures:
• fractional distillation

nodes.title: Rf Values
nodes.description: understand how to use the calculation of Rf values to identify the components of a mixture

nodes.title: The Structure of the Atom
nodes.description: know the structure of an atom in terms of the positions, relative masses and relative charges of sub-atomic particles

nodes.title: Deducing Electronic Configurations
nodes.description: understand how to deduce the electronic configurations of the first 20 elements from their positions in the Periodic Table

nodes.title: Universal Indicator
nodes.description: describe the use of universal indicator to measure the approximate pH value of an aqueous solution

nodes.title: Calculate Percentage Yield
nodes.description: calculate percentage yield

nodes.title: Formation of Covalent Bonds
nodes.description: know that a covalent bond is formed between atoms by the sharing of a pair of electrons

nodes.title: Exothermic & Endothermic
nodes.description: know that chemical reactions in which heat energy is given out are described as exothermic, and those in which heat energy is taken in are described as endothermic

nodes.title: Arrangement of the Periodic Table
nodes.description: understand how elements are arranged in the Periodic Table: • in order of atomic number • in groups and periods.

nodes.title: Formation of Sulfur Dioxide
nodes.description: explain how the combustion of some impurities in hydrocarbon fuels results in the formation of sulfur dioxide

nodes.title: Identifying Mixtures
nodes.description: understand how a chromatogram provides information about the composition of a mixture

nodes.title: Conductivity & Ionic Compounds
nodes.description: know that ionic compounds do not conduct electricity when solid, but do conduct electricity when molten and in aqueous solution

nodes.title: The Three States of Matter
nodes.description: Understand the three states of matter in terms of the arrangement, movement & energy of the particles

nodes.title: Flame Tests
nodes.description:
describe how to carry out a flame test
know the colours formed in flame tests for these cations: 
• Li+ is red 
• Na+ is yellow 
• K+ is lilac 
• Ca2+ is orange-red 
• Cu2+ is blue-green.

nodes.title: Halogens & Alkanes
nodes.description: describe the reactions of alkanes with halogens in the presence of ultraviolet radiation, limited to mono-substitution knowledge of reaction mechanisms is not required

nodes.title: The Greenhouse Effect
nodes.description: know that carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas and that increasing amounts in the atmosphere may contribute to climate change

nodes.title: Crystallisation
nodes.description:
describe these experimental techniques for the separation of mixtures:
• crystallisation

nodes.title: Pure Substance vs Mixture
nodes.description: understand that a pure substance has a fixed melting and boiling point, but that a mixture may melt or boil over a range of temperatures

nodes.title: Giant Covalent Structures
nodes.description: explain why substances with giant covalent structures are solids with high melting and boiling points

nodes.title: Calculate Reacting Masses
nodes.description: calculate reacting masses using experimental data and chemical equations

nodes.title: Order of Reactivity
nodes.description: know the order of reactivity of these metals: potassium, sodium, lithium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium, zinc, iron, copper, silver, gold

nodes.title: Common Ions
nodes.description:
know the charges of these ions: 
• metals in Groups 1, 2 and 3
• non-metals in Groups 5, 6 and 7 
• Ag+, Cu2+, Fe2+, Fe3+, Pb2+, Zn2+
• hydrogen (H+), hydroxide (OH– ), ammonium (NH4 +), carbonate (CO3 2– ), nitrate (NO3 - ), sulfate (SO4 2– ).

nodes.title: Giant Ionic Lattices
nodes.description: understand why compounds with giant ionic lattices have high melting and boiling points

nodes.title: Metal Displacement Reactions
nodes.description:
understand how metals can be arranged in a reactivity series based on their displacement reactions between: 
• metals and metal oxides 
• metals and aqueous solutions of metal salts.

nodes.title: The Alkanes
nodes.description:
know the general formula for alkanes
explain why alkanes are classified as saturated hydrocarbons
understand how to draw the structural and displayed formulae for alkanes with up to five carbon atoms in the molecule, and to name the unbranched-chain isomers

nodes.title: Key Terms
nodes.description: know what is meant by the terms atomic number, mass number, isotopes and relative atomic mass (Ar)

nodes.title: Melting & Boiling Point Patterns
nodes.description: explain why the melting and boiling points of substances with simple molecular structures increase, in general, with increasing relative molecular mass

nodes.title: Classify an Element, Compound or Mixture
nodes.description: understand how to classify a substance as an element, compound or mixture

nodes.title: Formulae of Simple Compounds by Experiment
nodes.description: understand how the formulae of simple compounds can be obtained experimentally, including metal oxides, water and salts containing water of crystallisation

nodes.title: How Alkali Metals React with Water
nodes.description: understand how the similarities in the reactions of these elements with water provide evidence for their recognition as a family of elements

nodes.title: Metals Reacting with Water & Acids
nodes.description:
understand how metals can be arranged in a reactivity series based on their reactions with: 
• water 
• dilute hydrochloric or sulfuric acid.

nodes.title: Factors Affecting Rates
nodes.description: describe the effects of changes in surface area of a solid, concentration of a solution, pressure of a gas, temperature and the use of a catalyst on the rate of a reaction

nodes.title: Acids & Alkalis
nodes.description: know that acids in aqueous solution are a source of hydrogen ions and alkalis in a aqueous solution are a source of hydroxide ions

nodes.title: Explaining Rates
nodes.description: explain the effects of changes in surface area of a solid, concentration of a solution, pressure of a gas and temperature on the rate of a reaction in terms of particle collision theory

nodes.title: The Main Fractions
nodes.description:
know the names and uses of the main fractions obtained from crude oil: refinery gases, gasoline, kerosene, diesel, fuel oil and bitumen
know the trend in colour, boiling point and viscosity of the main fractions

nodes.title: Practical: Determine the Percentage of Oxygen in Air
nodes.description: practical: determine the approximate percentage by volume of oxygen in air using a metal or a non-metal

nodes.title: Formulae for Ionic Compounds
nodes.description: write formulae for compounds formed between the ions listed above

nodes.title: Practical: Determine the Formula of Copper(II)Oxide
nodes.description: practical: know how to determine the formula of a metal oxide by combustion (e.g. magnesium oxide) or by reduction (e.g. copper(II) oxide)

nodes.title: Cracking
nodes.description: describe how long-chain alkanes are converted to alkenes and shorter-chain alkanes by catalytic cracking (using silica or alumina as the catalyst and a temperature in the range of 600–700 ºC)

nodes.title: Deducing Monomers & Repeat Units
nodes.description: understand how to deduce the structure of a monomer from the repeat unit of an addition polymer and vice versa

nodes.title: Acid Rain
nodes.description: understand how sulfur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen oxides contribute to acid rain

nodes.title: Empirical & Molecular Formulae
nodes.description: know what is meant by the terms empirical formula and molecular formula

nodes.title: Formation of Nitrogen Oxides
nodes.description: know that, in car engines, the temperature reached is high enough to allow nitrogen and oxygen from air to react, forming oxides of nitrogen

nodes.title: Metals & Non-Metals in the Periodic Table
nodes.description: identify an element as a metal or a non-metal according to its position in the Periodic Table

nodes.title: Measuring Rates
nodes.description: describe experiments to investigate the effects of changes in surface area of a solid, concentration of a solution, temperature and the use of a catalyst on the rate of a reaction

nodes.title: Why Noble Gases are Unreactive
nodes.description: understand why the noble gases (Group 0) do not readily react

nodes.title: Practical: Investigate Paper Chromatography Using Inks & Food Colourings
nodes.description: practical: investigate paper chromatography using inks/food colourings

nodes.title: Calculate Molar Enthalpy Change
nodes.description: calculate the molar enthalpy change (ΔH) from the heat energy change, Q

nodes.title: Practical: Effect of Surface Area on Rate of Reaction
nodes.description: practical: investigate the effect of changing the surface area of marble chips and of changing the concentration of hydrochloric acid on the rate of reaction between marble chips and dilute hydrochloric acid

nodes.title: Similar Chemical Properties
nodes.description: understand why elements in the same group of the Periodic Table have similar chemical properties

nodes.title: Tests for Anions
nodes.description:
describe tests for these anions: 
• Cl– , Br– and I– using acidified silver nitrate solution 
• SO4 2– using acidified barium chloride solution 
• CO3 2– using hydrochloric acid and identifying the gas evolved.

nodes.title: Relative Formula Mass & Relative Molecular Mass
nodes.description: calculate relative formula masses (including relative molecular masses) (Mr) from relative atomic masses (Ar)

nodes.title: Oxidation & Reduction
nodes.description:
understand the terms: in terms of gain or loss of oxygen and loss or gain of electrons. 
• oxidation 
• reduction 
• redox 
• oxidising agent

nodes.title: The pH Scale
nodes.description: understand how to use the pH scale, from 0–14, can be used to classify solutions as strongly acidic (0–3), weakly acidic (4–6), neutral (7), weakly alkaline (8–10) and strongly alkaline (11–14)

nodes.title: Predicting Properties in Group 1
nodes.description: use knowledge of trends in Group 1 to predict the properties of other alkali metals

nodes.title: Prepare a Soluble Salt
nodes.description: describe an experiment to prepare a pure, dry sample of a soluble salt, starting from an insoluble reactant

nodes.title: Interconversion Between the States of Matter
nodes.description:
Understand the interconversions between the three states of matter in terms of:
- the names of the interconversions
- how they are achieved
- the changes in arrangement, movement & energy of the particles

nodes.title: Simple Molecular Structures
nodes.description:
explain why substances with a simple molecular structures are gases or liquids, or solids with low melting and boiling points the term intermolecular forces of attraction can be used to represent all forces between molecules.
explain how the structure of C60 fullerene influences its physical properties, including electrical conductivity and hardness

nodes.title: Moles-Mass Calculations
nodes.description: understand how to carry out calculations involving amount of substance, relative atomic mass (Ar) and relative formula mass (Mr)

nodes.title: Practical: Investigate Metals Reacting with Acids
nodes.description: practical: investigate reactions between dilute hydrochloric and sulfuric acids and metals (e.g. magnesium, zinc and iron)

nodes.title: Calculate Relative Atomic Mass
nodes.description: be able to calculate the relative atomic mass of an element (Ar) from isotopic abundances

nodes.title: Electrostatic Attractions
nodes.description: understand covalent bonds in terms of electrostatic attractions

nodes.title: Filtration
nodes.description:
describe these experimental techniques for the separation of mixtures:
 • filtration

nodes.title: Naming Organic Compounds
nodes.description: understand how to name compounds relevant to this specification using the rules of International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) nomenclature students will be expected to name compounds containing up to six carbon atoms

nodes.title: Simple Distillation
nodes.description:
describe these experimental techniques for the separation of mixtures: 
• simple distillation

nodes.title: Catalysts & Rates
nodes.description:
know that a catalyst is a substance that increases the rate of a reaction, but is chemically unchanged at the end of the reaction
know that a catalyst works by providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy

nodes.title: Drawing Polymers
nodes.description: understand how to draw the repeat unit of an addition polymer, including poly(ethene), poly(propene), poly(chloroethene) and (poly)tetrafluoroethene

nodes.title: Physical Properties
nodes.description: know the colours, physical states (at room temperature) and trends in physical properties of these elements

nodes.title: Trends in Group 1
nodes.description: understand how the differences between the reactions of these elements with air and water provide evidence for the trend in reactivity in Group 1

nodes.title: Practical: Prepare Copper(II) Sulfate
nodes.description: practical: prepare a sample of pure, dry hydrated copper(II) sulfate crystals starting from copper(II) oxide

nodes.title: Tests for Cations
nodes.description:
describe tests for these cations: 
• NH4 + using sodium hydroxide solution and identifying the gas evolved 
• Cu2+, Fe2+ and Fe3+ using sodium hydroxide solution.

nodes.title: Practical: Investigating Temperature Changes
nodes.description:
practical: investigate temperature changes accompanying some of the following types of change: 
• salts dissolving in water 
• neutralisation reactions 
• displacement reactions 
• combustion reactions

nodes.title: Ionic bonding
nodes.description: understand ionic bonding in terms of electrostatic attractions

nodes.title: Paper Chromatography
nodes.description:
describe these experimental techniques for the separation of mixtures: 
• paper chromatography.

nodes.title: Combustion
nodes.description: describe the combustion of elements in oxygen, including magnesium, hydrogen and sulfur

nodes.title: Crude Oil & Fractional Distillation
nodes.description:
know that crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons
describe how the industrial process of fractional distillation separates crude oil into fractions

nodes.title: Classifying Organic Reactions
nodes.description:
understand how to classify reactions of organic compounds as substitution, addition and combustion 
knowledge of reaction mechanisms is not required

nodes.title: Solubility Rules
nodes.description:
know the general rules for predicting the solubility of ionic compounds in water: 
• common sodium, potassium and ammonium compounds are soluble 
• all nitrates are soluble 
• common chlorides are soluble, except those of silver and lead(II) 
• common sulfates are soluble, except for those of barium, calcium and lead(II) 
• common carbonates are insoluble, except for those of sodium, potassium and ammonium 
• common hydroxides are insoluble except for those of sodium, potassium and calcium (calcium hydroxide is slightly soluble).

nodes.title: Two Colour Indicators
nodes.description: describe the use of litmus, phenolphthalein and methyl orange to distinguish between acidic and alkaline solutions

nodes.title: Monomers
nodes.description: know that an addition polymer is formed by joining up many small molecules called monomers

nodes.title: Calculate Empirical & Molecular Formulae
nodes.description: calculate empirical and molecular formulae from experimental data

nodes.title: Reversible Reactions
nodes.description:
know that some reactions are reversible and this is indicated by the symbol ⇌ in equations
describe reversible reactions such as the dehydration of hydrated copper(II) sulfate and the effect of heat on ammonium chloride

nodes.title: Calculate Heat Energy Change
nodes.description: calculate the heat energy change from a measured temperature change using the expression Q = mcΔT

nodes.title: Calorimetry
nodes.description: describe simple calorimetry experiments for reactions such as combustion, displacement, dissolving and neutralisation

nodes.title: Fraction Supply & Demand
nodes.description: explain why cracking is necessary, in terms of the balance between supply and demand for different fractions

nodes.title: Solutions Terminology
nodes.description:
know what is meant by the terms: 
• solvent 
• solute 
• solution 
• saturated solution.

nodes.title: Ionic Bonds: Dot & Cross Diagrams
nodes.description: draw dot-and-cross diagrams to show the formation of ionic compounds by electron transfer, limited to combinations of elements from Groups 1, 2, 3 and 5, 6, 7 only outer electrons need be shown

nodes.title: Finding the Percentage of Oxygen
nodes.description: understand how to determine the percentage by volume of oxygen in air using experiments involving the reactions of metals (e.g. iron) and non-metals (e.g. phosphorus) with air

nodes.title: Neutralisation
nodes.description: know that alkalis can neutralise acids

nodes.title: Disposal of Addition Polymers
nodes.description:
explain problems in the disposal of addition polymers, including: 
• their inertness and inability to biodegrade 
• the production of toxic gases when they are burned.

nodes.title: Diamond & Graphite
nodes.description: explain how the structures of diamond and graphite influence their physical properties, including electrical conductivity and hardness

nodes.title: Practical: Determine the Formula of Magnesium Oxide
nodes.description: practical: know how to determine the formula of a metal oxide by combustion (e.g. magnesium oxide) or by reduction (e.g. copper(II) oxide)

nodes.title: Writing Equations
nodes.description:
write word equations and balanced chemical equations (including state symbols): 
• for reactions studied in this specification 
• for unfamiliar reactions where suitable information is provided.
